challenges.title: Robots Are Rude
challenges.description:
A student project went to production with the staging notes still attached.

The developers were kind enough to publish a `robots.txt` asking crawlers to stay away from the interesting parts. Search engines listen. You don't have to.

**Target:** a local mirror is provided as an attachment — no live host is involved.

hints.text: Disallow rules are a map, not a lock.
Fetch the path that the file asks crawlers not to index.

challenges.title: View Source, Win Prize
challenges.description:
The club's first landing page shipped in a hurry. The developer left a note for a colleague, then forgot it existed.

Browsers render what you see. They ship what you don't. Find the note.

hints.text: Ctrl+U is a tool, not a cheat.

challenges.title: Cookie Monsta
challenges.description:
The dashboard decides who you are by reading a cookie it wrote itself:

```
session=eyJ1c2VyIjoic3R1ZGVudCIsInJvbGUiOiJ1c2VyIn0=
```

The admin panel is at `/admin`. The app trusts the cookie completely — which is the whole problem.

**Goal:** reconstruct a cookie that gets you the admin view and read the flag rendered there.

hints.text: That string is not encrypted, only encoded.
Change the role value, then re-encode the JSON exactly as the server expects it.

challenges.title: Injection Junction
challenges.description:
An internal staff portal still concatenates user input into its login query:

```sql
SELECT id, role FROM users WHERE email = '<input>' AND password = '<input>'
```

No WAF, no prepared statements, and a very confident comment in the code review.

**Goal:** authenticate as the first administrator, then read the flag from their profile.

hints.text: You do not need a password if the query never gets to check one.
Comment out the rest of the statement. In SQLite, `--` works.

challenges.title: Gatekeeper
challenges.description:
Our internal API uses JSON Web Tokens. The verifier was written by a third-party library that supports the `none` algorithm for "testing purposes".

You are given a valid low-privilege token and the API contract. The flag lives behind `GET /api/v1/admin/flag`.

**Goal:** forge a token with `role: admin` that the server accepts.

hints.text: Decode the three segments. The middle one is the claim set.
Try deleting the signature segment entirely, trailing dot included, and watch which error message disappears.
